why: #178 through a separator SHELL_OPERATORS does not carry. A newline separates two commands exactly as `&&` does, but shlex.split erases it — so `"true\nfalse"` and the argv ["true","false"] split to the same words, and a receipt for a run that executed only `true` (with `false` swallowed as its argument) passed as the whole gate. The paired case is stop-17, which pins the `&&` spelling that was already guarded; this is the spelling a consumer writing a two-step gate is most likely to reach for.
